observation.failure: All eight cases failed the unexpected-read boundary; desktop legacy additionally timed out showing Profile after reload. Both CJK cases recorded one uncaught error fingerprint.
observation.uncertainty: The first guard logged request kinds and page-error fingerprints only, so the exact blocked URL and uncaught error messages are unobserved. Google Fonts are a source-supported candidate, not established by this run.
observation.harnessIssue: Playwright added its default error-context Markdown metadata to each failed case, so the controller rejected the boundary attachment count. The inline boundary bodies are preserved in the raw JSON and extracted here; error-context file contents were not retained.
observation.processLabelQualification: The historical process executable field can contain a bounded Chromium process-title prefix with role flags; it is not a full argv or environment capture.

proofLimits: Eight private authored-browser scenarios exercise the actual public deployment, not existing user data, API writes, providers or a full product acceptance.
The only installed JavaScript tool is Playwright 1.61.1 in owned external runner storage. Chromium Linux system packages are installed on the disposable runner and are not independently uninstalled.

Direct child exit/close/EOF and original groups are checked. Same-UID Linux browser processes are additionally attributed by the unique owned binary/profile/cache path and kernel starttime; unreadable or uncertain attribution prevents owned-root deletion. This is not a host-wide process inventory.
Registry/browser downloads and allowed public hosted GETs are setup/acceptance network traffic, not a network sandbox. Userspace deadlines cannot interrupt blocked kernel filesystem calls.
